purpose: Extend the R1 mechanism study with CF03 request-presentation, CF05 control-world/side-channel, CF06 cross-layer-consistency, and CF07 multi-profile observations using neutral/read-only probes.

cf03RequestPresentation.finding: The complete observed main-document request header set and order were identical across all three arms.

consoleSideEffectProbe.finding: This detector family did not discriminate any arm on Chromium 153.0.8010.12 and must not be used as evidence in this environment.

executionContextProbe.finding: Both arms exposed the same execution-context structure. The Playwright utility-world suffix differed as an invocation identity, but Browserless/Puppeteer did not leave an additional world in this measurement.

remainingOpen: Browserless/Puppeteer internal CDP-domain subscriptions may still differ without producing a page-visible world delta.
Runtime/Console domain state cannot be inferred from the negative page probe alone.
Browserless source-level Network.enable/listener behavior remains provenance, not proven challenge causality.

sharedMismatch.note: This mismatch is shared by direct and Browserless arms under the current Network-v2 namespace; it is not a Browserless-specific discriminator and is not established as a provider challenge cause.

examples.browserless_DejaVu_Sans_resolution: DejaVu Sans from container Linux fonts

fontEnvironment.interpretation: The Browserless container and direct host Chromium present materially different font fingerprints despite using the same Chromium binary and network namespace.

cf07SessionProfile.finding: Three distinct persistent profiles all reached the same challenge standing while their substrates were healthy. This weakens a single-profile-local-corruption explanation but does not distinguish shared network, launch, provider-policy, or common session-history causes.

modelUpdate.CF03: No request header-set/order difference observed between current Browserless and direct controls in the local lab.
modelUpdate.CF05: Two page-visible detector families failed to distinguish Browserless from direct Playwright. Broader protocol-domain differences remain open but must not be inferred from project reputation alone.
modelUpdate.CF06: A shared KR-network vs Asia/Shanghai-timezone mismatch exists. Browserless also has route-specific window geometry and font-environment differences caused by its containerized presentation substrate.
modelUpdate.CF07: All three persistent carriers are independently challenge-gated; a one-profile failure is less plausible.
modelUpdate.CF08: Challenge remains an observed outcome only; no R2 result establishes the provider-authoritative cause.

explicitNonClaims: R2 does not show that any observed mismatch is sufficient to trigger Cloudflare or ChatGPT challenge policy.
R2 does not show that changing timezone, fonts, launch flags, network route, or control layer would make the protected provider admissible.
R2 does not automate or recommend solving, clicking, or bypassing a provider challenge.
R2 does not treat negative detector probes as proof that Runtime/Console/CDP state is invisible.
